structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, no native (non-introduced) amphibian species (frogs, toads, newts, i.e. Anura and Caudata) occurs on any truly oceanic island, meaning one of volcanic or coral origin that was never connected to a continent.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using a list of oceanic islands fixed before looking at the data (Hawaii, Galápagos, Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands, Cape Verde, St Helena, Ascension, Tristan da Cunha, Bermuda, Mauritius, Réunion, Marquesas, Society Islands, Cook Islands, Samoa, Tonga, Marianas, Kerguelen, São Tomé and Príncipe, Fiji), the number of native Anura or Caudata species recorded on them is 0. A single native species on one island counts as a counterexample. A count of 0 confirms the claim as stated ('strictly true'). Species flagged as introduced do not count.
structured_output.fail_criterion: At least 1 native Anura or Caudata species is recorded on at least 1 island of the pre-registered oceanic list, after excluding species whose AmphibiaWeb account says they are introduced. Examples to check are São Tomé and Príncipe and Fiji. Under this threshold the claim 'strictly true' is refuted. If the count is 1 to 3 islands with only a few species, the claim is a rough generalization that fails the strict reading.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'Batrachians (frogs, toads, newts)' maps to the orders Anura and Caudata. Caecilians (Gymnophiona) were not part of his claim and are excluded. 'Oceanic islands' is read in the modern geological sense of islands never joined to a continent. Continental fragments such as New Zealand, the granitic Seychelles, Madagascar and the Solomons are excluded because they are not oceanic. 'Naturally absent' maps to no native species in the distribution or country fields. Introduced species are identified from the species accounts. The mechanism claims (seawater kills spawn, introduced frogs thrive) are not tested by this plan. Introduced frogs thriving could be checked separately with GBIF establishmentMeans data. Modern reinterpretation: Darwin's claim was about island groups. Here it is tested species by species and island by island against current taxonomy and ranges.

dataset.name: AmphibiaWeb
dataset.why_it_fits: AmphibiaWeb is a global database of amphibian species. It offers downloadable species lists and per-species pages with country and geographic distribution fields, and these also state when a species is introduced. The fields used are order (Anura or Caudata), species, country or distribution, and the native or introduced note. Species are filtered to the pre-registered oceanic islands and checked against the pass and fail thresholds.
